name: Browser extension | Notelet
tagline: Notes and to-dos for each page and each site, in Chrome's side panel or Firefox's sidebar.
popTagline: Built to keep notes about a page where they belong: next to it.
popOverview: A browser extension for keeping notes and to-dos next to the page they relate to. Its panel is a Nutin application mounted without the router, published on both Chrome and Firefox from a single codebase, through the stores' reviews.

sectionKeyPoints.Two browsers, one source: Chrome's side panel and Firefox's sidebar: Firefox's manifest is derived from Chrome's at build time.

sectionKeyPoints.Stable keys: Addresses are normalized before being used as keys (no fragment, no tracking parameters).

sectionKeyPoints.Local or synced: Storage can switch between local and synced, with an item-by-item merge when sync is turned on.

sectionKeyPoints.Faking browser APIs in tests: Application tests run against a fake of the extension APIs, which can also behave like Firefox: storage and tab logic is tested without a browser.

sectionKeyPoints.Reproducible packages: The same sources give the same archive, byte for byte, and CI checks it with a second build.

sectionKeyPoints.A release pipeline with approval: A version tag creates the GitHub release, then store submissions wait for manual approval; third-party actions are pinned to commit hashes.

sectionKeyPoints.Concurrent windows: Each window has its own panel, saving on its own: two windows changing the same list at the very same moment can lose one change.

sectionKeyPoints.Sync conflicts: Browser sync keeps one entry per list, so the last write wins between two computers; turning sync on merges lists item by item instead.

sectionKeyPoints.A dense, keyboard-heavy interface: The panel had to stay accessible while packing many actions into a small space.
